text:
Olen Zellweger went back to Anaheim on Oct. 29 for the first time since the trade, and the Buffalo News and The Hockey News both made a story of it. What's more interesting is what Buffalo has done with him: his ice time is up almost four minutes over his last ten games, to over 21 a night.

The Sabres are better for it. They take 55% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five with Zellweger on the ice, nearly eight points better than without him, the best gap of any regular on this team. He has 3 goals on 1.68 expected, which will cool, and 6 points in 15 games.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking from last season explains the style: he gets to the home-plate area in front of the net at a 97th percentile rate for a defenseman and does a third of his shooting off the rush. His burst speed sits in the 99th percentile. Evolving-Hockey had him 49th among 215 defensemen last season. At 23, this looks like a player getting the role he was waiting for. We project about 31 points.
headline: Zellweger has found his minutes
